_meta.name: DSS Cup Lock (steel, 122 cm, imperial bays)
_meta.family: Cuplock 1.22 m, imperial bays 5-10 ft (node 0.50 m)
_meta.note: US cuplock (DSS / Blue Steel catalogue 12/2025) as a facade scaffold: 4' (1.219 m) horizontal as transom, imperial bays 5'-10', five 9" low-profile steel planks per bay, cups at 0.5 m, 2.0 m lift. 'verified' = false everywhere.
sources: 1067929480-BLUE-STEEL-DSS-03220-System-Scaffold-Catalog-12302025.pdf p.9 (tube 48.3 x 3.25 / 2.50), p.10 (verticals), p.11 (horizontals), p.13 (clamp braces for a 2 m drop), p.18 (California guardrail, not used)
1067929480-BLUE-STEEL-DSS-03220-System-Scaffold-Catalog-12302025.pdf p.41 (system jack BPSJB), p.49 (universal toe boards), p.58 (Twist Lock tube), p.60 (right angle clamp)
1067929480-BLUE-STEEL-DSS-03220-System-Scaffold-Catalog-12302025.pdf p.81 (9" raised-hook steel plank), p.83-84 (9" low-profile steel plank), p.97 (28" hatch plank with ladder)
approvals: No system approval named for Cup Lock; factories ISO 9001:2008, most EN 1090-1/2 EXC3 and EN ISO 3834-2 (catalogue)
changes: The catalogue's 'MM' columns hold metres; converted to mm. Imperial originals kept in the descriptions (lb values in 'mass_orig' where the extract has them).
Width = 4' horizontal CLH40 (1.219 m) as transom: 5 x 229 mm planks = 1145 mm in 1171 mm clear. DSS does not name a standard facade width; the metric CLH41 (1.25 m) would also take 5 planks.

Bays = imperial series 5'-10' (1.524-3.048 m), short bays 3' and 4'. Every bay has a horizontal (p.11), plank (p.83-84), toe board (p.49) and clamp brace (p.13). CLCB30/40/60 are marked 'not stocked' (*) but have published weights and are used.

Plank, toe board and hatch catalogue lengths differ by a few mm from the horizontal bay lengths (e.g. WBDEP8 2440 vs CLH80 2438; GRUSTB toe boards are clear lengths); they are keyed to the bay length, the printed length is in l_printed_mm.
Guard rails = horizontals at the cups (standard cuplock practice). DSS also sells the clamp-on California guardrail CLGR (heavier, p.18), not used.

Two deck grades: 9" low-profile steel plank WBDEP (default; DSS's Cup Lock plank is WBDEP43CL) and 9" raised-hook steel plank WBSSP. Aluminium 9.5" walkboards (241 mm) do not fit 5 to a 4' bay and are left out.
Access: 28" (711 mm) hatch plank with aluminium ladder, 7' and 10' (p.97) + 2 planks of 229 mm beside it (1169 mm in 1171 mm clear: tight, check).
End guard rail = 2 x CLH40; end toeboard = GRUSTB40 (1140 mm; description printed 3'-9" in the catalogue, code 40).
System jack BPSJB: overall 0.54 m, max extension 0.38 m (p.41).
Tie = Twist Lock tube TL4 (1.22 m, 4.3 kg, p.58) and right angle clamps CMPRA (1.5 kg, p.60). No eyebolt in the catalogue: 0.2 kg estimated (Plettac value).

rules_verified.note: DSS gives no tie pattern, bracing frequency or wall gap: all placeholders. Jack travel 0.38 m is from the catalogue (p.41, BPSJB). Swivel jacks: anchors must hold 4 x the shear force on the slope, above 45 deg consult a Professional Engineer (p.41). For comparison only (other manufacturer): the SGB Cuplok user guide (339768111, p.2-3, 6-15) asks for a tie at every standard, vertically every 8 m (2 m lifts, pattern A) down to 4.5 m, and one braced bay in every 8 bays (20 m). Not applied here because it is not this manufacturer's document.
